_README: The single source of the book's structure; the build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. For an EPUB source, author it from book.draft.json (produced by scripts/ingest_epub.py) — refine the titles, add English titles, and MERGE or SPLIT units where the source EPUB's file boundaries do not match its logical chapters. Chapter ids MUST start with 'ch' (ch01, ch02, ...). A chapter is treated as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists.
_deliverable_note: [SET PER PROJECT] The EPUB filename. Builder, qa_epub and the Stop hook all read this; never rely on the default.
_source_note: The source is a digital EPUB with reliable text (no OCR). Record its title/edition and anything notable (missing chapters, embedded notes, image-heavy sections) here.
_metadata_note: Optional richer metadata, all read by the builder: subtitle_en; title_file_as / author_file_as (library sort keys; default to the display forms); translator_en; publication_date (ISO, else year-01-01); rights; source_ref (a dc:source line naming the source edition); subjects (a JSON list; legacy singular 'subject' still honored); series + series_index (calibre metas and the EPUB3 collection); language (default 'en'); source_language (BCP-47, e.g. 'zh'); source_script (lang tag for source-script spans, e.g. 'zh-Hant' or 'zh-Hans'; default 'zh'); cover_image (a file under the project or data/ dirs, copied byte-identical); modified (deterministic dcterms:modified stamp, default 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z -- rebuilds are byte-identical); deliverable (output path used when the builder/qa get no argv); uid (kept verbatim unless it is a malformed urn:uuid, which is replaced by a deterministic UUIDv5 of title_en). The source book's own notes go in source_notes.json, a second stream kept separate from the translator's notes.json.
_translator_note: Optional. A list of paragraph strings rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note back-matter page. Inline ... is honored; use NUMERIC character references (—,  ), never named entities. If omitted, a generic method note is generated.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 中文書名, made from the digital source EPUB.
Say here what the register decisions were, who the author is, and how any editorial choices (the source's own notes, ambiguous passages, cut material) were handled.
_structure_note: One entry per chapter, in reading order. Each chapter: id (ch01..), chapter (int), title (source), title_en, and OPTIONAL 'part' (a label like 'Part One. ...'; consecutive chapters sharing it are grouped in the TOC). Keep 'src' (the source spine href, optionally with #anchor) and 'chars' (source character count, from ingest) so the survey can size batches; 'text_file' points at the extracted source text for that unit. Each section: id (ch01s01..), section (int), title, title_en, src, chars, and an OPTIONAL 'subsections' list (id ch01s01x1.., title, title_en). The reading markdown uses '## ' for the chapter (h1), '### ' per section (h2, matched to these section ids in order), '#### ' per subsection (h3, matched to the subsection ids in order). Fill in the WHOLE structure up front: the survey and the skeleton EPUB are built from it before any translation.

structure.part: Part One. English Part Title (optional; omit if the book has no parts)
structure.title: 第一章 章名

subsections.title: 一 小節名
subsections.title_en: i. English Subsection Title (optional; omit the whole list if none)

_batches_note: Your work plan (proposed by scripts/survey.py, approved by the commissioner). Informational, but keeping it here lets a fresh session see the plan. first_section/last_section are section ids.
